He is the Mighty﴾ in what He withholds, ﴿the Wise﴾ in what He releases.

Al-Imam Abu al-Hasan Abd al-Rahman ibn Muhammad al-Dawudi informed us, saying: Abu al-Hasan Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Salt informed us, saying: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Abd al-Samad al-Hashimi informed us, saying: Ubayd Allah ibn Asbat informed us, saying: my father informed us, saying: Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr informed us, from Warrad, from al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to say after every obligatory prayer: "There is no god but Allah alone, with no partner. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verses 6–8:

﴿Indeed, Satan is an enemy to you, so take him as an enemy.﴾ That is: oppose him by obeying Allah, and do not obey him. ﴿He only invites his party﴾ that is, his followers and allies, ﴿to be among the companions of the Blaze.﴾ That is: so that they will be in the Blaze. Then he described the condition of those who agree with him and those who oppose him, saying: ﴿Those who disbelieve will have a severe punishment, but those who believe and do righteous deeds will have forgiveness and a great reward.﴾

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Is one whose evil deed has been made attractive to him so that he sees it as good...﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl and the polytheists of Makkah.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it was revealed concerning the people of desires (ahl al-ahwa') and innovations (ahl al-bid'a). [[See: Zad al-Masir: 6 / 475.]]

Qatadah said: among them are the Kharijites (al-Khawarij, an early sect that declared Muslims who committed grave sins to be unbelievers and made their blood and property lawful), who consider the blood and property of the Muslims lawful. As for the people of major sins (ahl al-kaba'ir), they are not among them, because they do not consider major sins lawful.

﴿Is one for whom...﴾ was made to appear attractive, adorned and beautified, ﴿his evil deed, [so that] he sees it as good...﴾ That is: his ugly deed. ﴿...so he sees it as good.﴾ Satan adorned that for him through whispering.

In the verse there is an ellipsis, and its meaning is: "Is one for whom his evil deed was made attractive, so that he sees falsehood as truth, like one whom Allah has guided, so that he sees truth as truth and falsehood as falsehood?" ﴿Indeed, Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills.﴾

It is also said: its answer is under His saying, ﴿So do not let yourself go to waste in regret over them﴾. Its meaning would then be: "Is one for whom his evil deed was made attractive and whom Allah has led astray, [then] your soul goes to waste in regret over him?" That is: you grieve over him, so do not let your soul go to waste in regrets over them.

Al-Husayn ibn al-Fadl said: there is inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in it. Its meaning is: "Is one for whom his evil deed was made attractive, so that he sees it as good, [so] do not let your soul go to waste in regret over them. Indeed, Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills." Al-hasrah is the intensity of grief over what has passed of the matter. The meaning of the verse is: do not grieve over their disbelief and their destruction if they do not believe.

Abu Ja'far recited: "fa-la tudhhib" with a damma on the ta' and a kasra on the ha', and "nafsaka" (your soul) in the accusative. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Knowing of what they do.﴾

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verses 9–10:**

﴿It is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds, and We drive them to a dead land, and We revive the earth thereby after its death. Thus will be the resurrection﴾, meaning from the graves.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Whoever desires honor—to Allah belongs all honor﴾. Al-Farra' said: the meaning of the verse is: whoever wants to know to whom honor belongs, then to Allah belongs all honor. [See: Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra': 2/367.]

Qatadah said: "Whoever desires honor, let him seek honor through obedience to Allah." The meaning is the call to obedience to the One who possesses honor, i.e., let him seek honor from Allah by obeying Him. [See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 7/303.] This is like saying: "Whoever wants wealth, the wealth belongs to so-and-so," i.e., let him seek it from him. This is because the disbelievers worshipped idols and sought honor through them, as Allah says: ﴿And they have taken gods besides Allah that they may be for them a source of honor. No!﴾ [Maryam: 81], and He says: ﴿Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do they seek honor with them? Indeed, all honor belongs to Allah﴾ [al-Nisa': 139].

﴿To Him ascends the good word﴾, i.e., to Allah. The good word is His saying: "There is no god but Allah." It was also said that it is the statement of a person: "Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the Greatest."

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliji informed us, Abu Mansur al-Sam'ani informed us, Abu Ja'far al-Rayyani informed us, Humayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us, al-Hajjaj ibn Nasr informed us, al-Mas'udi informed us, from Abd Allah ibn al-Mahariq, from his father, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "When I narrate to you a hadith, I will show you its confirmation from the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: No Muslim servant says five words—'Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, Allah is the Greatest, and blessed is Allah'—except that an angel takes them and places them beneath his wing, then ascends with them. He does not pass with them over a company of angels except that they seek forgiveness for the one who said them, until they reach the Face of the Lord of the worlds." Its confirmation from the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is His saying: ﴿To Him ascends the good word﴾. This was mentioned by Ibn Mas'ud. [Narrated by al-Tabari: 22/120; al-Hakim authenticated it: 2/425, and al-Dhahabi agreed. Also by al-Bayhaqi in al-Asma' wa'l-Sifat: 2/34. al-Suyuti attributed it additionally to Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Tabarani. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/8–9.]

It was also said: "the good word" is the remembrance of Allah. And from Qatadah: "To Him ascends the good word," i.e., Allah accepts the good word.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And righteous deed raises it﴾, i.e., righteous deed raises the good word. The pronoun in His saying "yarfa'uhu" (يَرْفَعُهُ, "raises it") refers back to the good word. This is the view of Ibn Abbas, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan, Ikrimah, and most of the exegetes (mufassirun).

Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: the good word is the remembrance of Allah, and righteous deed is performing His obligations. Whoever remembers Allah but does not perform His obligations, his words are returned upon his deeds. [This part was narrated by al-Tabari: 22/121 from Ibn Abbas.] Faith is not by wishful thinking nor by outward adornment, but is what settles in the hearts and is confirmed by deeds. Whoever speaks well but acts unrighteously, Allah rejects his words. Whoever speaks well and acts righteously, the deed raises it. That is because Allah says: ﴿To Him ascends the good word, and righteous deed raises it﴾. [al-Suyuti attributed this in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/10 to Abd ibn Humayd, and to al-Bayhaqi from al-Hasan.] A hadith has also come: "Allah does not accept a statement except with a deed, nor a statement or deed except with an intention." [Ibn Hajar said in al-Kafi al-Shaf, pp. 138–139: It was narrated by al-Khatib in al-Jami' from the transmission of Baqiyyah ibn Isma'il ibn Abd Allah, from Aban, from Anas, as a marfu' report. Aban is abandoned (matruk). It has another route from Abu Hurayrah as a marfu' report, narrated by Ibn Adi and Ibn Hibban, both in al-Du'afa', from Khalid ibn Abd al-Da'im, from Nafi' ibn Yazid, from Zuhrah ibn Ma'bad, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from him, with the wording "A Qur'an recited in prayer is better than a Qur'an recited outside prayer," and the hadith continues: "and there is no power except through deed," until its end. Ibn Hibban also narrated it from the transmission of al-Zuhri, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Ibn Mas'ud. In it is Ahmad ibn al-Hasan al-Misri, who is a liar.]

Others said: the pronoun in His saying "yarfa'uhu" refers to the righteous deed [meaning: the good word raises the righteous deed], so no deed is accepted unless it proceeds from tawhid (monotheism, the affirmation of Allah's oneness). This is the meaning of the statement of al-Kalbi and Muqatil.

It was also said: the raising is an attribute of Allah, Mighty and Majestic; its meaning is: righteous deed is raised by Allah, Mighty and Majestic. [Here the manuscript marker 90/b appears.]

Sufyan ibn Uyaynah said: righteous deed is sincere deed (al-ikhlas), meaning that sincerity is the cause of the acceptance of good acts, whether of speech or action. Its evidence is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿So let him who hopes for the meeting with his Lord do righteous deeds and not associate anyone in the worship of his Lord﴾ [al-Kahf: 110]. So He made the opposite of righteous deed to be shirk (association of partners with Allah) and riya' (showing off).

﴿And those who plot evil deeds﴾. Al-Kalbi said: i.e., those who commit evil deeds. Muqatil said: meaning shirk. Abu al-Aliyah said: meaning those who plotted against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) in Dar al-Nadwah, as Allah, Exalted, says: ﴿And [recall] when those who disbelieved plotted against you to restrain you﴾ [al-Anfal: 30].

Mujahid and Shahr ibn Hawshab said: they are the people of riya' (showing off). [See these views in: Ibn Kathir: 3/550; al-Bahr al-Muhit: 7/304; al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/10.]

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verses 9–10:**

﴿It is Allah who sends the winds, and they stir up clouds, and We drive them to a dead land, and We revive the earth thereby after its death. Thus will be the resurrection﴾, meaning from the graves.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿Whoever desires honor—to Allah belongs all honor﴾. Al-Farra' said: the meaning of the verse is: whoever wants to know to whom honor belongs, then to Allah belongs all honor. [See: Ma'ani al-Qur'an by al-Farra': 2/367.]

Qatadah said: "Whoever desires honor, let him seek honor through obedience to Allah." The meaning is the call to obedience to the One who possesses honor, i.e., let him seek honor from Allah by obeying Him. [See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 7/303.] This is like saying: "Whoever wants wealth, the wealth belongs to so-and-so," i.e., let him seek it from him. This is because the disbelievers worshipped idols and sought honor through them, as Allah says: ﴿And they have taken gods besides Allah that they may be for them a source of honor. No!﴾ [Maryam: 81], and He says: ﴿Those who take the disbelievers as allies instead of the believers. Do they seek honor with them? Indeed, all honor belongs to Allah﴾ [al-Nisa': 139].

﴿To Him ascends the good word﴾, i.e., to Allah. The good word is His saying: "There is no god but Allah." It was also said that it is the statement of a person: "Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, and Allah is the Greatest."

Abd al-Wahid al-Maliji informed us, Abu Mansur al-Sam'ani informed us, Abu Ja'far al-Rayyani informed us, Humayd ibn Zanjawayh informed us, al-Hajjaj ibn Nasr informed us, al-Mas'udi informed us, from Abd Allah ibn al-Mahariq, from his father, from Ibn Mas'ud, who said: "When I narrate to you a hadith, I will show you its confirmation from the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic: No Muslim servant says five words—'Glory be to Allah, praise be to Allah, there is no god but Allah, Allah is the Greatest, and blessed is Allah'—except that an angel takes them and places them beneath his wing, then ascends with them. He does not pass with them over a company of angels except that they seek forgiveness for the one who said them, until they reach the Face of the Lord of the worlds." Its confirmation from the Book of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, is His saying: ﴿To Him ascends the good word﴾. This was mentioned by Ibn Mas'ud. [Narrated by al-Tabari: 22/120; al-Hakim authenticated it: 2/425, and al-Dhahabi agreed. It was also said: "the good word" is the remembrance of Allah. And from Qatadah: "To Him ascends the good word," i.e., Allah accepts the good word.

His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿And righteous deed raises it﴾, i.e., righteous deed raises the good word. The pronoun in His saying "yarfa'uhu" (يَرْفَعُهُ, "raises it") refers back to the good word. Al-Hasan and Qatadah said: the good word is the remembrance of Allah, and righteous deed is performing His obligations. Whoever remembers Allah but does not perform His obligations, his words are returned upon his deeds. [This part was narrated by al-Tabari: 22/121 from Ibn Abbas.] Faith is not by wishful thinking nor by outward adornment, but is what settles in the hearts and is confirmed by deeds. Whoever speaks well but acts unrighteously, Allah rejects his words. Whoever speaks well and acts righteously, the deed raises it. That is because Allah says: ﴿To Him ascends the good word, and righteous deed raises it﴾. [al-Suyuti attributed this in al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/10 to Abd ibn Humayd, and to al-Bayhaqi from al-Hasan.] A hadith has also come: "Allah does not accept a statement except with a deed, nor a statement or deed except with an intention." Aban is abandoned (matruk). It has another route from Abu Hurayrah as a marfu' report, narrated by Ibn Adi and Ibn Hibban, both in al-Du'afa', from Khalid ibn Abd al-Da'im, from Nafi' ibn Yazid, from Zuhrah ibn Ma'bad, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from him, with the wording "A Qur'an recited in prayer is better than a Qur'an recited outside prayer," and the hadith continues: "and there is no power except through deed," until its end. Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verses 11–12:

His saying, Exalted and Mighty is He: ﴿And Allah created you from dust﴾ meaning: Adam; ﴿then from a drop of semen﴾ meaning: his offspring; ﴿then He made you into pairs﴾, males and females. ﴿No female conceives or gives birth except with His knowledge. **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 35, verses 13–18:**

﴿He causes the night to enter into the day, and causes the day to enter into the night, and has subjected the sun and the moon, each running for a term appointed. That is Allah, your Lord; to Him belongs the dominion. And those you invoke besides Him do not possess even a qitmir.﴾ That is, the idols. *Qitmir* is the thin covering of the date-pit, the delicate skin that lies over the pit.

﴿If you invoke them, they do not hear your call; and if they heard, they would not respond to you.﴾ That is, if you invoke the idols, they do not hear your supplication, and even if they heard, they would not answer you. ﴿And on the Day of Resurrection they will disavow your association.﴾ They will disown you and your worship of them, saying: "You did not worship us."

﴿And none can inform you like one who is Acquainted.﴾ That is, Himself. Meaning: no one can inform you like me, the All-Aware, the Knower of things.

﴿O mankind, you are the poor toward Allah﴾ in need of Allah's bounty. *Faqir* means one who is in need. ﴿And Allah is the Rich, the Praiseworthy.﴾ Rich above His creation, praised for His kindness toward them.

﴿If He wills, He can remove you and bring a new creation. And that is not difficult for Allah﴾ not hard, i.e., not mighty-difficult.

﴿And no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another. And if a heavily laden soul calls [another] to its load﴾ that is, a soul burdened with its sins calls someone else, ﴿to carry any of it, none will be carried, even if he should be a close relative.﴾ That is, even if the one called is a relative: his son, his father, his mother, or his brother. Ibn Abbas said: the father and mother will meet their son and say, "O my son, carry for me some of my sins," and he will say, "I cannot; my own burden is enough for me."

﴿You can only warn those who fear their Lord unseen﴾ who fear, ﴿their Lord﴾ while not having seen Him. Al-Akhfash said: its interpretation is that your warning benefits only those who fear their Lord unseen. ﴿And establish prayer. And whoever purifies himself﴾ acts righteously and does good, ﴿purifies himself only for his own benefit﴾ its reward belongs to him. ﴿And to Allah is the final destination.﴾

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verses 19–26:**

﴿And the blind and the seeing are not alike﴾. He means: the ignorant and the knowledgeable. It was also said: the blind to guidance and the one who sees guidance, that is, the believer and the polytheist.

﴿Nor are the darknesses and the light﴾. He means: disbelief and faith.

﴿Nor the shade and the scorching heat﴾. He means: Paradise and Hell. Ibn 'Abbas said: "al-harur" is the hot wind at night, and "al-samum" is the hot wind by day. It was also said: "al-harur" occurs by day together with the sun.

﴿Nor are the living and the dead alike﴾. He means: the believers and the disbelievers. It was also said: the scholars and the ignorant.

﴿Indeed, Allah makes hear whom He wills﴾, until he takes heed and responds. ﴿But you cannot make hear those who are in the graves﴾. He means: the disbelievers. He likened them to the dead in graves when they did not respond.

﴿You are only a warner﴾. You are only a warner who frightens them with the Fire.

﴿Indeed, We have sent you with the truth as a bringer of good tidings and a warner. And there is no nation but that a warner has passed among them﴾, that is, a nation in the past ﴿but that a warner had passed among them﴾, a prophet who warned.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verses 27–28:

﴿Do you not see that Allah sends down water from the sky, and We bring forth with it fruits of varying colours? And among the mountains are white and red streaks of varying colours, and [others that are] intensely black.﴾ *Judad* (streaks) means paths and tracts, its singular being *juddah*, like *mudda* and *mudad*. ﴿White and red, of varying colours, and intensely black﴾ means: *sudun gharabib* (intensely black) with the words inverted, so that the sense is *sud gharabib*. It is said: *aswad ghirbib* (intensely black), meaning very black, likened to the colour of the crow. That is, *tara'iq sud* (black streaks).

﴿And among mankind, the beasts, and the cattle are [things] of varying colours.﴾ He used the pronoun (*al-kināya*, the pronominal reference) in the masculine singular, *hu* in *ulwānuhu*, for the sake of *min* (of). It was also said: the pronoun refers back to what is implied, and the meaning is: *wa min al-nās wa al-dawābb wa al-an'ām mā huwa mukhtalif alwānuhu* (and among mankind, beasts and cattle is that whose colours vary). ﴿Thus﴾ means: just as the colours of the fruits and the mountains vary. Here the speech is complete; then it begins anew, saying: ﴿Only those among His servants who have knowledge fear Allah.﴾ Ibn 'Abbas said: it means that only those among My creation fear Me who know My majesty, My might, and My authority.

ʿAbd al-Wahid al-Maliḥi related to us, Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi related to us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf related to us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us, ʿUmar ibn Hafs related to us, al-A'mash related to us, Muslim related to us, from Masruq, from ʿĀ'isha (may Allah be pleased with her), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did something and allowed it, but some people abstained from it. This reached the Prophet (ﷺ), so he delivered a sermon, praised Allah, and then said: "What is wrong with people who abstain from something I do? By Allah, I am the one among them who knows Allah best and who fears Him most." [Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-I'tisam, chapter: What is disliked of excessive depth, dispute, extremism in religion and innovation: 13/276; and Muslim in al-Fada'il, chapter: his (ﷺ) knowledge of Allah the Exalted and the intensity of his fear, no. 2356, 4/1829; and the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 1/199–200.]

The Prophet (ﷺ) also said: "If you knew what I know, you would laugh little and weep much." [A part of a hadith narrated by al-Bukhari in Tafsir, the commentary on surah al-Ma'ida, chapter: the saying of Allah the Exalted: (Do not ask about things which, if made known to you, would trouble you), 8/280; and Muslim in al-Fada'il, chapter: his (ﷺ) veneration and avoiding excessive questioning about what is not necessary, no. 2359, 4/1823; and the author in Sharh al-Sunna: 14/368–369.]

Masruq said: Fear of Allah is sufficient knowledge, and being deceived about Allah is sufficient ignorance. A man said to al-Sha'bi: "Give me a fatwa, O scholar." Al-Sha'bi said: "The scholar is only the one who fears Allah, the Mighty and Majestic."

﴿Indeed Allah is All-Mighty, All-Forgiving.﴾ That is: Mighty in His dominion, Forgiving of the sins of His servants.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verses 29–32:**

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah﴾, meaning: those who recite [[Addition from manuscript "B".]] the Qur'an, ﴿and establish prayer and spend from what We have provided them, secretly and openly, hoping for a commerce that will never perish﴾, meaning it will never be ruined and never be lost. By "commerce" is meant the reward that Allah has promised.

Al-Farra' said: His saying "hoping" is the answer (jawab) to His saying "Indeed, those who recite the Book of Allah."

﴿That He may give them their full rewards﴾, the recompense of their deeds with reward, ﴿and increase them from His bounty﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: That is, beyond the reward, [such things] that no eye has seen and no ear has heard. ﴿Indeed, He is Forgiving and Appreciative﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: He forgives their great sins and appreciates their small deeds.

﴿And that which We have revealed to you of the Book﴾, meaning: the Qur'an, ﴿is the truth, confirming what is before it﴾ of the [other] books. ﴿Indeed, Allah is, concerning His servants, Acquainted and Seeing﴾. ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book﴾, meaning: the Book which We sent down to you, which was mentioned in the first verse, which is the Qur'an; We made it reach ﴿those whom We have chosen from Our servants﴾.

It is permissible that "then" (thumma) here carries the meaning of "and" (waw), i.e., "and We caused to inherit," like His saying: ﴿Then he was among those who believed﴾ [al-Balad: 17], i.e., "and he was among those who believed." The meaning of "We caused to inherit" is "We gave," because inheritance is a gift. This was said by Mujahid.

It was also said: "We caused to inherit" means "We delayed," and from this comes the word "inheritance" (mirath), because it is delayed until after the deceased. Its meaning is: We delayed the Qur'an from the earlier nations and gave it to you, and We made you fit for it.

﴿Those whom We have chosen from Our servants﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: He means the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ. Then He divided them and arranged them, saying: ﴿So among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds﴾. It was narrated from Usamah ibn Zayd concerning His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: "So among them is one who wrongs himself," the verse, that he said: The Prophet ﷺ said: "All of them are from this Ummah." [[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Kabir: 1/131, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Ba'th; in its chain is Muhammad ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Layla, who has poor memorization. See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/24; Majma' al-Zawa'id: 7/96.]]

Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us; Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us; al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed me; Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Qadi informed us; Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi informed us; Abu Qilabah informed us; 'Amr ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, from al-Fadl ibn 'Umayrah, from Maymun al-Kurdi, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, who said: I heard 'Umar ibn al-Khattab reciting on the pulpit: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from Our servants﴾, the verse, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Our foremost is foremost, our moderate one is saved, and our wrongdoer is forgiven." The exegetes differed concerning the meaning of "the wrongdoer," "the moderate," and "the foremost."

Ahmad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Salihi informed us; Abu Sa'id Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Sayrafi informed us; Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn 'Abd Allah al-Saffar informed us; Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Isa al-Bartí narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us; Sufyan informed us, from al-A'mash, from a man, from Abu Thabit, that a man entered the mosque and said: "O Allah, have mercy on my estrangement, console my loneliness, and send me a righteous companion." Abu al-Darda' said: "If you are truthful, then I am more fortunate with you than you are. As for the moderate, he will be reckoned with an easy reckoning. As for the one who wrongs himself, he will be detained at the station until distress reaches him, then he will enter Paradise." She said: "My son, they are all in Paradise. Mujahid, al-Hasan, and Qatadah said: ﴿So among them is one who wrongs himself﴾ refers to the companions of the left (ashab al-mash'amah), ﴿and among them is one who is moderate﴾ refers to the companions of the right (ashab al-maymanah), ﴿and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds [by the permission of Allah]﴾ [[What is between the brackets is an addition from manuscript "B".]] refers to the foremost, the drawn near, of all people. The meaning of "We caused to inherit" is "We gave," because inheritance is a gift. This was said by Mujahid.

It was also said: "We caused to inherit" means "We delayed," and from this comes the word "inheritance" (mirath), because it is delayed until after the deceased. Its meaning is: We delayed the Qur'an from the earlier nations and gave it to you, and We made you fit for it.

﴿Those whom We have chosen from Our servants﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: He means the Ummah of Muhammad ﷺ. Then He divided them and arranged them, saying: ﴿So among them is one who wrongs himself, and among them is one who is moderate, and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds﴾. Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us; Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us; al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed me; Muhammad ibn 'Ali ibn al-Husayn al-Qadi informed us; Bakr ibn Muhammad al-Marwazi informed us; Abu Qilabah informed us; 'Amr ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, from al-Fadl ibn 'Umayrah, from Maymun al-Kurdi, from Abu 'Uthman al-Nahdi, who said: I heard 'Umar ibn al-Khattab reciting on the pulpit: ﴿Then We caused to inherit the Book those whom We have chosen from Our servants﴾, the verse, and he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Our foremost is foremost, our moderate one is saved, and our wrongdoer is forgiven." Mujahid, al-Hasan, and Qatadah said: ﴿So among them is one who wrongs himself﴾ refers to the companions of the left (ashab al-mash'amah), ﴿and among them is one who is moderate﴾ refers to the companions of the right (ashab al-maymanah), ﴿and among them is one who is foremost in good deeds [by the permission of Allah]﴾ [[What is between the brackets is an addition from manuscript "B".]] refers to the foremost, the drawn near, of all people. [[See: al-Tabari: 22/135.]]

It is narrated from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: The foremost is the sincere believer; the moderate is the showy one (al-mura'i); and the wrongdoer is the disbeliever in Allah's blessing who does not deny it, because He judged all three to enter Paradise, saying: ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence, they will enter them﴾.

Some of them said, and this is mentioned from al-Hasan: The foremost is the one whose good deeds outweigh his bad deeds; the moderate is the one whose good and bad deeds are equal; and the wrongdoer is the one whose bad deeds outweigh his good deeds. [[See: Zad al-Masir: 7/489–490.]]

It was also said: The wrongdoer is one whose outward appearance is better than his inward state; the moderate is one whose outward and inward are equal; and the foremost is one whose inward state is better than his outward appearance.

It was also said: The wrongdoer is one who professes the oneness of Allah with his tongue but whose actions do not match his words; the moderate is one who professes the oneness of Allah with his tongue and obeys Him with his limbs; and the foremost is one who professes the oneness of Allah with his tongue, obeys Him with his limbs, and makes his deeds sincerely for Him.

It was also said: The wrongdoer is the one who recites the Qur'an; the moderate is the one who recites it and knows it; and the foremost is the one who recites it, knows it, and acts upon what is in it.

It was also said: The wrongdoers are the people of the major sins (kaba'ir); the moderate are the people of the minor sins (saghair); and the foremost is the one who has committed neither a major nor a minor sin.

Sahl ibn 'Abd Allah said: The foremost is the scholar; the moderate is the student; and the wrongdoer is the ignorant.

Ja'far al-Sadiq said: He began with the wrongdoers, informing that one draws near to Him only through His generosity, and that wrongdoing does not prevent one from being chosen. Then He followed with the moderate, because they are between fear and hope. Then He concluded with the foremost, so that no one would feel secure from His plan, and all of them are in Paradise.

Abu Bakr al-Warraq said: He arranged them in this order according to the stations of people, because the states of the servant are three: disobedience, heedlessness, then repentance, then nearness. When he disobeys, he enters the category of the wrongdoers; when he repents, he enters the body of the moderate; and when his repentance is sound and his worship and striving increase, he enters the ranks of the foremost.

Some of them said: The meaning of the wrongdoer is the disbeliever; this was mentioned by al-Kalbi.

It was also said: The intended meaning is the hypocrite. According to this view, the wrongdoer does not enter into His saying: "Gardens of perpetual residence, they will enter them." This speaker interpreted "chosen" as chosen in creation, in the sending of a messenger to them, and in the sending down of the Book. However, the first view is the well-known one, that the intended meaning of all of them is the believers, and this is the position of the majority of the people of knowledge.

His saying: ﴿And among them is one who is foremost in good deeds﴾, meaning: foremost to Paradise, or to the mercy of Allah, by good deeds, that is, by righteous actions. ﴿By permission of Allah﴾, meaning: by the command of Allah and His will. ﴿That is the great bounty﴾, meaning: His causing them to inherit the Book.

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verses 33–34:

Then He informed of their reward, saying: ﴿Gardens of perpetual residence (Adn) which they will enter﴾, meaning the three categories. Abu 'Amr recited "yudkhalūnahā" (they will be made to enter), with a ḍamma on the yā' and a fatḥa on the khā', while the others recited it with a fatḥa on the yā' and a ḍamma on the khā' (they enter). ﴿They will be adorned therein with bracelets of gold and pearls, and their clothing therein will be silk.﴾ ﴿And they will say﴾, i.e., and they will say when they enter Paradise: ﴿"All praise is due to Allah, who has removed from us the grief."﴾ Al-ḥazan (grief) and al-ḥuzn are one and the same, like al-bakhal and al-bukhl (stinginess). Ibn 'Abbas said: "The grief of the Fire." Qatadah said: "The grief of death." Muqatil said: "They grieved because they did not know what Allah would do with them." 'Ikrimah said: "The grief of sins and misdeeds, and the fear that their acts of obedience would be rejected." Al-Qasim said: "The grief of the loss of blessings, the turning of the heart, and the fear of the outcome." It was also said: "The grief of the terrors of the Day of Resurrection." Al-Kalbi said: "What used to grieve them in the world concerning the matter of the Day of Resurrection." Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "The worry over bread in this world." It was also said: "The worry of livelihood." Al-Zajjaj said: "Allah removes from the people of Paradise all griefs, whether they concern livelihood or the Hereafter."

Abu al-Hasan 'Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Dahhak al-Khatib informed us, saying: Abu Ishaq Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Isfara'ini related to us, saying: Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Isma'ili informed us, saying: Abu al-'Abbas Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Turabi informed us, saying: Yahya ibn 'Abd al-Hamid related to us, saying: 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam related to us, from his father, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "There is no loneliness for the people of "There is no god but Allah" in their graves nor in their gathering place. As if I could see the people of "There is no god but Allah" shaking the dust from their heads, saying: 'All praise is due to Allah, who has removed from us the grief.'" [[The Hafiz Ibn Hajar said in al-Kafi al-Shaf (p. 139): "It was narrated by Abu Ya'la, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Bayhaqi in the beginning of al-Shu'ab, and al-Tabarani in al-Awsat, from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar. In it is 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, who is weak. It has another route with al-Tabarani and al-Nasa'i in al-Kuna from Ibn 'Umar, and another with al-Bayhaqi in al-Shu'ab. And on the subject there is a report from Ibn 'Abbas narrated by Tammam in his Fawa'id and al-Khatib in the biography of Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Ta'ifi, and from Anas in Ibn Mardawayh." See also: Ibn Kathir: 3/558.]]

It is also said: the death will not be decreed upon them so that they die, like His saying: "They will cry out, 'O Malik, let your Lord put an end to us!'" [al-Zukhruf: 77], meaning, let Him decree death upon us so that we may rest. ﴿Nor will its punishment be lightened for them﴾, that is, the punishment of the Fire. ﴿Thus do We recompense every ungrateful one﴾, every disbeliever. Abu 'Amr recited "yujza" (with the ya', with a damma on it, and a fatha on the zay), with "kull" in the nominative, on the form of the passive voice (ghayr tasmiyat al-fa'il). The others recited "najzi" (with the nun, with a fatha on it, and a kasra on the zay), with "kull" in the accusative.

﴿And they will cry out therein﴾, that is, they will call for help and shout. The verb "yasṭarikhūna" is of the form "yaftaʿilūna", derived from "al-ṣurākh", which is the shouting. They will say: ﴿Our Lord, bring us out﴾ from it, from the Fire, ﴿that we may do righteousness, other than what we used to do﴾ in the world, of polytheism (shirk, associating partners with Allah) and evil deeds. Then Allah will say to them, as a rebuke: ﴿Did We not give you a life long enough that whoever would be mindful might be mindful therein?﴾ It has been said that this refers to reaching maturity. ʿAṭāʾ, Qatadah and al-Kalbi said: eighteen years. al-Hasan said: forty years. Ibn ʿAbbas said: sixty years, and this is reported from ʿAli. It is the lifespan by which Allah, the Exalted, left no excuse for the son of Adam.

Abdul-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Ahmad ibn ʿAbdullah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, Muhammad ibn Isma'il informed us, ʿAbd al-Salam ibn Mutahhar informed us, ʿUmar ibn ʿAli narrated to us, from Ma'n ibn Muhammad al-Ghifari, from Sa'id ibn Abi Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Allah, the Exalted, has left no excuse for a man whose term He delayed until He brought him to sixty years." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-Riqaq, chapter: "Whoever reaches sixty years, Allah has left no excuse for him regarding his lifespan": 11/238.]]

Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us, Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us, al-Husayn ibn Muhammad ibn Fanjawayh informed us, Ahmad ibn Ja'far ibn Himdan narrated to us, Ibrahim ibn Sahawayh narrated to us, al-Hasan ibn ʿArafah narrated to us, al-Muharibi informed us, from Muhammad ibn ʿAmr, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The lifespans of my ummah are between sixty and seventy years, and few of them surpass that." [[Narrated by al-Tirmidhi in al-Zuhd, chapter: "What has come concerning the lifespans of this ummah...": 6/6, and he said: "This is a hasan gharib hadith" from the narration of Abu Salih from Abu Hurayrah, and it has been narrated through other routes from Abu Hurayrah. Also Ibn Majah in al-Zuhd, chapter: "Hope and the term": 2/1415, and al-Hakim authenticated it: 2/427, according to the condition of Muslim, and al-Dhahabi agreed with him. Also Ibn Hibban in Mawarid al-Zaman no. (2467) p. 611, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan: 3/370. The Hafiz rated its chain as hasan in Fath al-Bari: 11/240. ﴿And there came to you the warner﴾. It means Muhammad (ﷺ). This is the view of most exegetes. It has also been said that it refers to the Qur'an. ʿIkrimah, Sufyan ibn ʿUyaynah and Waki' said: it is grey hair. The meaning is: Did We not give you a life long enough until you grew grey? It is said: grey hair is a warner of death. And in a report: No hair turns white except that it says to its sister: "Prepare yourself, for death has drawn near."

﴿So taste, for the wrongdoers have no helper.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 38–39:

﴿Indeed, Allah is the Knower of the unseen of the heavens and the earth; indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts.﴾ ﴿It is He who has made you successors upon the earth.﴾ That is: some of you succeed others. It is also said: He made you a nation that succeeded those before it, and it saw in those before it what it should take as a lesson.

﴿Whoever disbelieves, upon him is his disbelief.﴾ That is: upon him is the burden of his disbelief. ﴿And the disbelief of the disbelievers does not increase them, in the sight of their Lord, except in hatred.﴾ That is, in anger. ﴿And the disbelief of the disbelievers does not increase them except in loss.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 35, verse 40–42:

﴿Say: "Have you considered your partners whom you invoke besides Allah?"﴾ That is, you made them My partners by your claim, meaning the idols. ﴿Show me what they have created of the earth, or do they have a share in the heavens? Or have We given them a Book?﴾ Muqatil said: Have We given the disbelievers of Makkah a Book? ﴿So they are upon clear proof from it.﴾ Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, Hamzah and Hafs recited "bayyinah" (clear proof) in the singular, while the others recited "bayyinat" (clear proofs) in the plural. It means: clear evidences from it, from the various kinds of clarification found in that Book.

﴿Nay, the wrongdoers promise one another nothing but delusion.﴾ That is, they promise nothing but (what) ... Ghurur (delusion) is that which deceives a person and has no basis. Muqatil said: It means that what Satan promises the disbelievers of the children of Adam, namely the intercession of the gods on their behalf in the Hereafter, is delusion and falsehood. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, Allah holds the heavens and the earth lest they should cease;﴾ that is, lest they cease. ﴿And if they should cease, none could hold them after Him;﴾ that is, none holds them after Him, meaning none other than Him. ﴿Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving.﴾ If it is asked: what is the meaning of mentioning forbearance here? It is said: because the heavens and the earth were about to do what they were about to do regarding the punishment of the disbelievers, so Allah, exalted is He, held them from ceasing by His forbearance and forgiveness, in that He did not treat them with punishment.

﴿And they swore by Allah with their most emphatic oaths﴾ meaning: the disbelievers of Makkah, when word reached them that the People of the Book had denied their messengers, they said: "May Allah curse the Jews and the Christians! Messengers came to them and they denied them." And they swore by Allah and said: "If a messenger came to us, we would surely be better guided than any of them." That was before the mission of the Prophet ﷺ. When Muhammad was sent, they denied him, so Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿And they swore by Allah with their most emphatic oaths that if a warner came to them, they would surely be better guided than any of the (other) nations﴾ [[See: al-Bahr al-Muhit: 7/318.]] a messenger, ﴿…than any one of the nations.﴾

That is, of the Jews and the Christians. ﴿But when a warner came to them﴾ Muhammad ﷺ, ﴿it increased them in nothing but aversion.﴾ That is, his coming increased them only in distance from guidance.

﴿Istikbaran fi al-ard﴾ ("arrogantly in the land"): "istikbaran" is in the accusative as a *badal* (substitute, in apposition) for "nufur" (aversion).

﴿Wa makr al-sayyi'﴾ ("and the evil scheming"): meaning the evil deed. The noun "makr" (scheming) is attributed to its qualifier. Al-Kalbi said: it is their gathering together upon polytheism and the killing of the Prophet (ﷺ).

Hamzah recited "makr al-sayyi'" with the hamza silent, as a lightening (*takhfif*). This is also the recitation of al-A'mash.

﴿Wa la yahiq al-makr al-sayyi'﴾ ("and the evil scheming does not encompass"): that is, the evil scheming does not befall or surround.

﴿Illa bi-ahlihi﴾ ("except its people"): so they were killed on the day of Badr. Ibn 'Abbas said: the consequence of polytheism does not befall anyone except the one who committed polytheism. The meaning is: the burden of their scheming returns upon them.

﴿Fa-hal yanzuruna﴾ ("Do they then await"): that is, they expect.

﴿Illa sunnata al-awwalin﴾ ("except the way of the former peoples"): except that the punishment descends upon them as it descended upon the disbelievers who passed before.

﴿Fa-lan tajida li-sunnati Allah tabdila wa-lan tajida li-sunnati Allah tahwila﴾ ("So you will not find any change in the way of Allah, and you will not find any alteration in the way of Allah").

﴿Awa lam yasiru fi al-ard fa-yanzuru kayfa kana 'aqibatu alladhina min qablihim wa-kanu ashadda minhum quwwatan wa-ma kana Allah li-yu'jizahu﴾ ("Have they not travelled in the land and seen how was the end of those before them, though they were greater than them in strength? Nor is there anything in the heavens or on earth that could cause Allah to fail"): meaning, so that it would escape Him.

﴿Min shay'in fi al-samawati wa-la fi al-ard innahu kana 'Aliman Qadiran﴾ ("He is ever Knowing, All-Powerful").

﴿Wa-law yu'akhidhu Allahu al-nas bi-ma kasabu﴾ ("And if Allah were to seize people for what they have earned"): from the crimes.

﴿Ma taraka 'ala zahriha﴾ ("He would not leave upon its back"): that is, upon the back of the earth. This is a metonymy for what has not been mentioned.

﴿Min dabbatin﴾ ("any creature"). As it was in the time of Noah, Allah destroyed everything upon the back of the earth except those who were in Noah's ship.

﴿Wa-lakin yu'akhkhiruhum ila ajalin musamman fa-idha ja'a ajaluhum fa-inna Allaha kana bi-'ibadihi Basiran﴾ ("But He defers them to an appointed term. And when their term comes, indeed Allah is ever Seeing of His servants").

Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, said: he means the people of His obedience and the people of His disobedience.
